title: Why I superset EVERYTHING (the giant sets principle)
summary: He supersets about 90% of his training as giant sets with no rest. The exception is the opening heavy compound strength work, where he rests and focuses. Giant sets save 30-40 minutes, double as cardio/GPP and don't hurt hypertrophy if pairings avoid overlapping muscles. He also uses deliberate overlap to pre-exhaust strong muscles so weak ones do the work.

claims.claim: He supersets about 90% of his training as giant sets: all exercises follow each other with no rest.

The exception is opening strength work: the big compound lift at lower reps that starts each session is not supersetted, and he rests fully between sets of squats, deadlifts or bench to keep his focus and energy on them.
Even heavy curls go into a giant set: curls, then shoulder raises, a forearm exercise, a back exercise and so on.
You could superset heavy bench with curls without hurting performance, but he doesn't because his bench is highly affected by his mental state and focus.
Supersetting everything saves 30-40 minutes per session.
Supersetting different muscles costs little stamina (biceps then shoulders); be careful pairing two lifts that use the same muscles, e.g. heavy grip work followed by pulls without straps.
Superset lower body lifts with something static, low-rep or not using the legs: front squats with leg raises or pull-ups is good, front squats with deficit deadlifts is terrible.
Giant sets act as GPP: they tax the cardiovascular system and spare you separate cardio.
Cardio isn't just running outside; any time your heart is pumping hard and your breath is short, that is cardio.
He supersets 300 lb rows with stiff-leg deadlifts despite both taxing the lower back, because his lower back is unusually big and resilient; this is an exception, not general advice.
He would never superset bench press with overhead press because it is too taxing on the rotator cuff, and his rotator cuffs are weak.
Know your strong and weak points and build superset pairings around them.
Use supersets to pre-exhaust dominant muscles: heavy rows pre-tire his glutes and lower back so his weak hamstrings must carry the following stiff-leg deadlifts, isolating them better.
You don't need to rest two minutes between sets of curls; superset them with shoulders, forearms or abs.
Most people should take as much rest as needed during strength work and superset all volume and accessory work.
Giant sets are not detrimental to performance or hypertrophy when used inside an intelligently written body part split.
